CHERNOBYL ANOMALOUS ZONE RESEARCH INSTITUTE (CAZRI)

Project “Hephaestus-M”

Author: Prof. N. S. Rozhkov
Subject: Notes on AER-2.5 calibration; field-test log for directed alloying and disassembly.
Operational status: Top secret. Clearance level V.

12.08.2012
First successful tests of the Anomalous Extractor-Resonator prototype 1.2. As expected, artifacts are ultra-dense clumps of deformed matter whose crystal lattices have been altered by extreme fields and resist standard molecular classification. Directed pulses destabilized the structure of the “Droplet.” At first it cracked. After extensive tuning, the AER produced a clean base substrate: fine dust named “A-Fraction.”
Observation: The substrate is extremely unstable. Two lab assistants suffered second- and third-degree burns. Special shielded transport capsules are required. The bunker’s steel floor was damaged.

(...)
28.05.2013
The event from three days ago has been classified as the Great Emission. It overturned all previous research. The sky over the Zone went black at once; instruments could not register the psi level. Nearly every research team at the Center died. The emission created the “Darkness,” a vast, impenetrable mist of unknown origin. It absorbs light, blocks radio signals and, worst of all, resonates with anomalous deformation throughout the Zone. Physics has changed. Familiar anomalies became unstable and new hybrid formations with immense energy appeared. Our understanding of the Exclusion Zone has been thrown back to the Stone Age.

(...)
15.08.2013
A disastrous chain of events. Since we cannot synthesize even rudimentary artifacts in the lab, I proposed using anomalies “tainted by the Darkness” as a natural forge and source of catalytic pulses. Yesterday we lost research team Petal-4 during a field synthesis attempt. A junior researcher fatally miscalculated the shielding matrix’s disintegration timing. Its heat-resistant shell collapsed before the A-Fraction fused with the artifact core. A cascade resonance followed. Only radioactive slag and melted equipment remained.
Management wants to shut down Hephaestus-M and may suspend its funding. I refused outright. We are too close to our goal to retreat because of incompetent lab staff.

(...)
02.11.2013
A breakthrough. I recalculated everything using the revised algorithm and designed a frame matrix able to withstand increased gravitational pressure and chaotic discharges from the new anomalies. Field operation in sector Y-14: we placed a depleted “Moonlight” and three portions of electrical A-Fraction in a shielding matrix, then set the glass matrix in the pulsing core of a distorted “Electra.” The perimeter teemed with mutated creatures showing anomalous electricity generation; the Zone may be reshaping local fauna for the new environment.
Sensors recorded a peak discharge. The matrix survived the critical first seconds, letting the environment fuse substrate and core, then burned out as expected. We found a stabilized artifact in the crater. Its energy capacity and dynamics exceed all known pre-emission samples by 263%. The method works.

(...)
14.02.2014
Attempt to build the second AER-2.4 prototype. This is the sixteenth operator this week. I do not ask where management finds them. Critical weakness: the Darkness causes constant background-radiation fluctuations. Unless the Extractor-Resonator pulse is calibrated to within thousandths, the artifact annihilates instead of splitting into A-Fraction. The resulting surge of anomalous energy is highly likely to kill the AER operator.
For reasonably safe operation, the calculation algorithms must be improved and the resonance system fully rebalanced. Addendum: correction data before each cycle must NEVER be entered manually.
[Further down: calibration data for the AER-2.5 prototype]

An anomalous substrate recreated by the AER unit’s targeted resonance with a biological/chemical artifact. It looks like a fine powder, dirty green, yellow or brown, with a foul smell that is hard to describe—somewhere between ozone, rotting organic matter and a laboratory reagent.\nRumors in the Zone claim this chemical dust can be used to synthesize not only artifacts but medicines, or even treat serious illnesses. Scientists remain skeptical and warn against experimenting with it, since it “may cause irreversible DNA deformation.”

An anomalous substrate recreated by the AER unit’s targeted resonance with an electrical artifact. The dust looks like a fine bluish powder with a metallic sheen. Microscopic sparks jump between particles whenever they move.\nContact with skin causes a noticeable but nonfatal electric shock. Some experienced stalkers use a pinch of this electrical substrate to “revive” old batteries or detectors. It works, but the devices remain functional only briefly afterward.

Fine anomalous substrate recreated by the AER unit’s targeted resonance with a gravitational artifact. Each particle creates a molecular-scale gravity anomaly, bending quantum space around itself for immeasurably brief moments.\nStalkers say inhaling this dust makes your body feel half as heavy for several minutes. Scientists strongly advise against testing the rumor: experiments rate its internal effects as “severe tissue damage”...

An anomalous substrate recreated by the AER unit’s targeted resonance with a fire-nature artifact. It looks like a bright orange powder flecked with white. Even a small amount gives off steady warmth.\nThe most valuable property of thermal A-Fraction is its ability to store and release heat, albeit unstably. Some Zone tinkerers use it at home: a single grain in a campfire warms a pot of stew faster and better than a gas burner. Don’t overdo it—a slightly larger amount reacts like a thermite grenade explosion.
The form of a future chemical artifact.\nPlace the matrix near a chemical anomaly to form the artifact.
This Shielding Matrix will transform at any location. If the artifact disappears, you’ll need a detector.
This Shielding Matrix will transform only in the Middle Belt or locations farther north. If the artifact disappears, you’ll need a detector.
This Shielding Matrix will transform only in northern locations or in the Dark regions. If the artifact disappears, you’ll need a detector.
The form of a future electrical artifact.\nPlace the matrix near an electrical anomaly to form the artifact.
A synthesized Shielding Matrix for a gravitational artifact, ready for the reaction.\nPlace the matrix near a gravitational anomaly to form the artifact.
The form of a future thermal artifact.\nPlace the matrix near a thermal anomaly to form the artifact.

Greetings! We have been working together for a long time, so I can share some information with you. Not long ago, a mercenary squad attacked our mobile group. The group was transporting a crucial report on the calibration of the AER-2.5 prototype, and during the firefight the only prototype of this installation was destroyed. If you manage to find the report, we can install a copy of the prototype in your shelter for a very modest fee. I have heard that a stash belonging to the mercenaries is somewhere in the Agroprom underground, but their main "stash-4" was compromised. So they most likely moved the document somewhere near the wastewater treatment plant, in the underground itself. Please search the underground and find that calibration report; without it, we cannot build a second prototype!

The AER unit can synthesize artifacts from A-Fraction. You can choose the amount and nature of A-Fraction to suit the desired result.\nAfter synthesis, you receive a matrix cocoon. Place it in an anomaly to finish the process. The reaction forms an artifact of the corresponding grade from the substrate. Its grade depends on the amount of A-Fraction used.\nSelect an artifact grade and type to begin synthesis.

The AER unit can break artifacts down into an anomalous substrate called A-Fraction. The resulting substrate has the same nature as the original artifact. A-Fraction can be used to alloy or synthesize artifacts of the corresponding nature.\nSelect an artifact to begin disassembly.

This encyclopedia shows which specimens have already been studied and how many artifacts remain unknown.\nIn “Artifact Grades,” you can filter the displayed artifacts. The columns group artifacts by their nature.\nSelect a tab above to choose how to process artifacts.

The AER unit can alloy (recreate) artifacts. An artifact is placed in a Shielding Matrix (cocoon), made from a base material and A-Fraction. To complete the process, place the matrix in an anomaly of the matching nature and class.\nAfter alloying, you receive a matrix cocoon. Place it in an anomaly to finish the process. After the reaction, the artifact’s class increases by +1. Example: a Class III (3) artifact becomes Class IV (4). Artifacts are limited to Class V (5).\nSelect an artifact to begin alloying.
